summary: Executed strict allowlist backend regression + live paid-model chat checks; updated outdated tests to current publisher-verified-only policy and ran targeted Notes UI validation on preview.

integration_issues.flow: Notes model-refresh 503 UX (without full page reload)
integration_issues.issue: Could not deterministically observe the inline error-banner transition when forcing /api/chat/models=503 via Playwright route during refresh-click path; unavailable state is visible when 503 is forced at reload time.

action_items: Main agent: self-verify refresh-click 503 UX path (no reload) for draft retention + explicit unavailable error state; automation route interception was inconsistent in this run.
Keep production allowlist strict (do not widen to satisfy old fixtures); only extend audited IDs after publisher evidence review.
critical_code_review_comments: Legacy tests were still asserting generic unmoderated/free-era IDs; they are now aligned to audited publisher-verified model identity and strict response-model verification.
Paid live-call volume guard is now respected in tests by skipping an extra paid integration case after equivalent coverage to avoid unnecessary spend.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend target suite result: 35 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. Live chat completion path succeeded with current default paid model and multi-turn same-session retention checks. UI confirmed paid-only notice text, single Dolphin option, correct publisher card href, and price units. Three attempts were made to automate refresh-click 503 handling; reload-time forced 503 clearly shows unavailable state, but click-path banner transition could not be captured deterministically.
rca of the issue: RCA (test-harness boundary): refresh-click 503 check likely impacted by timing/cache/service-worker behavior in preview, causing non-deterministic assertion timing for [data-testid='chat-error']. Network logs confirm forced 503 occurred. Mitigation: instrument client-side model-refresh promise outcome (or expose deterministic test hook) to assert state transition without relying only on timing-sensitive DOM observation.
